q-39432.name: Question 1
q-39432.problem: Given that $‖u‖=4$ and $u\cdot v=-16$, find the smallest possible value of $‖2v‖.$
q-39432.worked_solution:
Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|u\cdot v| & \le ‖u‖\cdot ‖v‖ \\ |-16| & \le 4\cdot ‖v‖ \\ 4 & \le ‖v‖.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply both sides of the inequality by $2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot 4 & \le 2\cdot ‖v‖ \\ 8 & \le ‖2v‖\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the minimum possible value of $‖2v‖$ is $8.$

q-40883.name: Question 4
q-40883.problem: Given that $‖u‖=5$ and $u\cdot v=-30$, find the smallest possible value of $‖3v‖.$
q-40883.worked_solution:
Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|u\cdot v| & \le ‖u‖\cdot ‖v‖ \\ |-30| & \le 5\cdot ‖v‖ \\ 6 & \le ‖v‖.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply both sides of the inequality by $3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3\cdot 6 & \le 3\cdot ‖v‖ \\ 18 & \le ‖3v‖\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the smallest possible value of $‖3v‖$ is $18.$

q-140440.name: Question 5
q-140440.problem: Given that $‖u‖=5$ and $u\cdot v=-15$, find the smallest possible value of $‖v‖.$
q-140440.worked_solution:
Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}|u\cdot v| & \le ‖u‖\cdot ‖v‖ \\ |-15| & \le 5\cdot ‖v‖ \\ 15 & \le 5\cdot ‖v‖.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply both sides of the inequality by $\frac{1}{5}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5}\cdot 15 & \le \frac{1}{5}\cdot 5\cdot ‖v‖ \\ 3 & \le ‖v‖\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the smallest possible value of $‖v‖$
is  $3.$
